verdict.rationale: Lorikeet Coach scores all conversations, AI and human, with a Ticket Quality Score against your quality standards, and it identifies bad scores. It also turns findings into fixes it can implement itself or suggest, which covers the scored-sample, flagged-failure and feedback-loop parts of the story. Guardrail events also land in analytics for QA review. All of this comes from vendor marketing pages. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of how the scoring rubric, failure flags and review workflow are configured, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a support ops lead, AI conversations get ongoing QA — scored samples, flagged failures, and a review loop that feeds fixes back into the agent

citations.quote: Coach's Ticket Quality Score reviews 100% of conversations against your quality standards, AI and human alike, replacing manual spot checks with full coverage.
Coach reviews 100% of tickets against your quality standards and turns findings into fixes, so your AI agent improves every week instead of drifting.
When Coach gives a conversation a bad score, we refund the AI portion of that interaction.
Coach can implement improvements on your behalf, or make suggestions for you to action yourself.
every event lands in your analytics as a tracked outcome your QA team can review
